lines.t: History of Eastern Wisconsin Stock Cars
Eastern Wisconsin Stock Cars, Inc. began as a sanctioning body in the year 1960. The name, however,
was discussed and voted on in the May 21, 1959 membership meeting with it being Eastern Wisconsin
Stock Car Association. Prior to 1960 Erwald Stock of Manitowoc was the promoter. The actual inception
of Eastern Wisconsin Stock Cars as a sanctioning body started at the March 7, 1960 membership meeting
when the VFW wanted the Association to co-promote the races at the Fairgrounds. At the next meeting,
however, the VFW decided not to take part in the promoting. Bob Akright and Gene Bonnett then said
they would promote the races if the Association could loan them $400 to get things started. At the May
meeting the club accepted Bob Akright and Harold Laack as the promoters. Gate admission in 1960 was
adults $1.00, 8-14 was $ .50, and under 8 free. Pit passes were $1.50.
In July of 1960 the club decided to divide up the money in the treasury at the end of the season and
give it to the drivers. Only enough money was kept in the treasury to start the races the following season.
Officers of the first EWSCA were Lanny Schirmer-President, Bob Akright-Vice President, and Kermit
Schulz was elected Secretary-Treasurer. In September of that year the club established a policy that
would require cars to race at half of the races or no point bonus. Also in that meeting the Chilton Fair
Board asked if the club would race there once a month if they built a quarter-mile track, and the club
agreed. EWSCA previously raced on the half mile. The first point payoff was held October 29, 1960 at
Starting in 1961, the Association decided to run the Chilton track on Wednesday nights. A car had to
complete at least half the races at each track to qualify for the point payoff. 1961 officers were President-
Harry Wiessgerber, Vice President-Terry Fee, and Secretary-Treasurer Kermit Schulz. Bob Akright and
Happy Laack were voted as track managers for both tracks. Four directors were added to the Board in
1961, the four being Harvey Miller, Marvin Halschback, Andy Lerchenko, and Bill Fitzgerald. In
September the club prohibited women from being in the pits and from being members. (These rulings
have since been changed). Spectator cars got their start during the 1961 racing season with no points
awarded. Prizes such as a jacket, oil, patches, or other merchandise were given. Point payoff party in
1961 was held at Andy's Place on October 28.
Board of directors in 1962 consisted of President Harry Wiessgerber, Vice President Don Diener,
Secretary Bernard Dineen, Treasurer Eldor Zander, and Board members Andy Levchenko, Harvey
Sportsmen rules were also being formed as the spectator class was getting out of hand, since they had
few rules. The sportsmen class was officially started in 1963 with the rules committee consisting of Russ
Waldron, Jim Eisner, Frank Kraus, Bob Akright, and Happy Laack. Some of the early stars in the
sportsmen division included Oscar Konen, Milt Schaeffer, Buck Carmen, Richard Hed, Russ Waldron,
LeRoy Dickmann, Ken Steffen, and Paul Ziegelbauer. Modified stars included Ken Markwardt, Carl
Kuhlow, Lanny Schirmer, Don Diener, Woody Klug, Ken Painter, Tom Sippel, and Bill Eickberg, just to
In 1967 the 1/4 oval at Plymouth was lengthened slightly and had new clay added. Hobby Stocks were
added to the program in 1970. During the first year the drivers ran for trophies and in 1971 were under
In 1972 EWSCA received a shot in the arm as many of the Milwaukee Stock Car Racing Association
started competing at the Plymouth and Chilton tracks. Two years later the club ended its twelve year
competition at the Chilton tracks. Special shows were run at the Calumet County fairgrounds in Chilton,
the most noted is the appearance of EWSCA at the fair.
In 1968, the club made weekly appearances at the 141 Speedway in Francis Creek. EWSCA
sanctioned races there for six years on Thursday nights and later Wednesday nights. With dwindling
fields of cars and added expenses the club stopped running in 1982 after membership approval.
Before the 1984 racing season the track at Plymouth moved fifty feet to the east and was lengthened
from a quarter mile to one-third mile. In 1985 a large metal grandstand was constructed which seated
4036 people. Besides Plymouth and Chilton, Eastern Wisconsin Stock Cars has sanctioned races at
Beaver Dam and Fond du Lac.
Membership has grown steadily through the years, from less than 100 in 1960 to over 1100 in 1989.
Over 100 drivers compete weekly in three divisions: modifieds, sportsmen, and hobby stock.
